task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Telangana woman dies in US road crash, family seeks help to bring back mortal remains
items.summary: A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Missouri, US, after a truck allegedly rammed the car she was travelling in. Daram Supriya, from Maripeda mandal in Mahabubabad district, was returning home after closing her restaurant in St Louis when the accident occurred, her family members told media. According to reports , the accident reportedly took place around 2.20 am on October 5. Supriya died on the spot, while her friend, another woman from Telangana who was travelling with her, sustained serious injuries and was shifted to a hospital for treatment. According to Supriya’s family, the two women were returning home in a car when a truck hit their vehicle from behind. Further details about the circumstances of the accident and the condition of the injured woman are awaited. Supriya had been running a restaurant in St Louis. She had married Kodumuri Ranjith, who works in the software sector, around five years ago. The couple has a two-and-a-half-year-old son. items.title: CM Satheesan seeks CPI(M) apology for calling Malappuram a ‘den of fundamentalists’
items.summary: A day after former CPI(M) MLA P Nandakumar described Malappuram as a “den of religious fundamentalists and communalists”, Keralam Chief Minister VD Satheesan on October 4, demanded an unconditional apology from the CPI(M), accusing the party of demonising the Muslim-majority district. In a post on X, Satheesan condemned Nandakumar’s remarks and said that they amounted to “communal slurs” against the people of Malappuram. He also criticised former Chief Minister and CPI(M) leader Pinarayi Vijayan for not objecting to the remarks when they were made in his presence. Satheesan said Pinarayi’s silence suggested the remarks had the “tacit endorsement” of the CPI(M). He accused the party of adopting “dog-whistle politics” by disparaging minority communities and alleged that its repeated criticism of Malappuram reflected an anti-minority shift. Satheesan also demanded that Pinarayi and the CPI(M) Central leadership clarify their position on Nandakumar’s remarks. He questioned the party’s claim to be a progressive and secular organisation and warned of strict action against those promoting communalism.
